options.text: $29$ stays circled as prime, while $1$ is crossed out and $27$ is crossed out as composite.
$1$ is circled as a prime because it is the first label on the list.
Each next uncrossed number is circled as prime and its later multiples are crossed out.
$25$ is found by dividing values in the list instead of crossing out multiples of $5$.

stem:
Anaya runs the Sieve of Eratosthenes on the whole numbers from $1$ to $30$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims are correct when the sieve is finished?

teacher.key_rationale: In the sieve, 1 is crossed out; each next uncrossed number is circled as prime and its multiples are crossed. 29 remains prime; 27 and 25 are struck as composites. 1 is not prime, and dividing is not the sieve step.
